what: docs/40_OPEN_SOURCE_LICENSES.md:3 asks the SBOM to name the versions and
licences of what this repository actually ships. docs/25_CICD_DEVOPS.md §23
item 10 asks CI to produce it. This manifest is the list of components
that MUST be findable when it is produced — one entry per dependency
docs/40 and the task books name by name — plus, for the names that are
genuinely not package dependencies of this tree, the witness that says
Every entry is checked by tests/security/check-sbom.py, and an entry whose
witness stops holding turns its row red. Two witness kinds exist because

witness_kinds.in-sbom: the component must appear in the named face's CycloneDX document (id matched as module path / group+name / pypi name)
witness_kinds.present-elsewhere: the thing is in the tree but not in any package SBOM (a container image, a code generator, a tool). Its `witness` command must print something, and what it prints appears in the row's evidence
witness_kinds.absent-from-tree: the SBOM key-component list names it but this tree does not depend on it. Its `witness` must print nothing — the moment the tree gains it, this entry goes red and the manifest has to be updated to require it in the SBOM

floors.what: A component count below these is a broken generation, not a small tree: an SBOM that lost its components would verify vacuously. Set well under today's count.

components.name: pgx (PostgreSQL driver)
components.why: CLAUDE.md §7 names pgx/sqlc as the canonical database access stack; sqlc generates against it (sqlc.yaml).

components.name: Go toolchain
components.why: The toolchain version is a build input, not a module dependency, so CycloneDX has no component for it; go.mod's `go` directive is its pin (CLAUDE.md §7: Go 1.27.x).

components.name: sqlc
components.why: A code generator, not a linked dependency: it is not in go.mod, so it is absent from the module SBOM. sqlc.yaml and infra/migrations/README.md carry its pin (v1.31.1), and tests/integration/check-sqlc-drift.sh is what holds the generated code to it.

components.name: chi
components.why: docs/40's key-component list names chi, and the correct answer for THIS tree is that it is not here: CLAUDE.md §7 says "net/http + chi 风格轻量路由", i.e. chi-STYLE routing on the standard library, and that is what the tree does. The witness is the evidence: a grep that must find nothing. Add chi as a real dependency and this entry turns red, which is the point — the manifest would then have to require it in the module SBOM.

components.name: Next.js
components.why: CLAUDE.md §7: Next.js 16 Active LTS is the frontend framework.

components.name: Primer React
components.why: CLAUDE.md §10 and §7: the UI is GitHub Primer, and @primer/react is the component library.

components.name: Octicons (Primer icons)
components.why: CLAUDE.md §7 names Primer/Octicons; this is the icon package the web app imports.

components.name: Playwright
components.why: The browser suites live in 13 separate npm projects under tests/ (each with its own package-lock.json), outside the pnpm workspace whose SBOM is .sbom/node.cdx.json — so this is a present-elsewhere entry, not a missing one. The witness prints one of the projects that pins it; today all 13 pin 1.55.0.

components.name: pymatgen
components.why: docs/40 and the adapter's own pyproject both say the scientific Python stack arrives with the adapter tasks; today the adapter's dependency list is literally empty, and its SBOM (6 components) is its dev tooling only. The witness asserts the empty list: the first scientific dependency added makes this entry red, and the manifest then has to require pymatgen in the Python SBOM.

components.name: ASE (Atomic Simulation Environment)
components.why: Same entry as pymatgen, and the same witness: ASE is named by docs/40 as a scientific dependency and is not in the tree yet. Kept as its own entry so the SBOM key-component list can name both without either one hiding the other.

components.name: PostgreSQL + pgvector
components.why: CLAUDE.md §7/§8: PostgreSQL + pgvector is the scientific truth store. It is a service image, not a package dependency, so no package SBOM carries it.

components.name: Redis
components.why: CLAUDE.md §7: Redis for cache/async. A service image, not a package dependency.
components.licence: RSALv2 / SSPLv1 (Redis 7.4 onwards) — commercial-restriction, NOT open source by OSI's definition

components.name: MinIO (S3-compatible blob store)
components.why: CLAUDE.md §7: S3-compatible blob storage, MinIO locally. A service image. Note the blob API contract is the S3 protocol, so the local container is an implementation choice rather than a code dependency.

components.name: Gitea
components.why: CLAUDE.md §7: internal Gitea behind the GitProvider adapter. A service image.

components.name: Mailpit (dev-stack mail sink)
components.why: The dev stack's SMTP sink (ops/DEV_COMMANDS.md:71, docs/64_UBUNTU_DEV_ENV.md:104). It runs only in the local compose stack, not in a deployment, but it is an image the tree pulls, so it is recorded here like the other four. Its licence is NOT verified by this tree: nothing in the repository states one and the check could not be performed offline. Recorded as `unknown` — which the licence audit prints as UNVERIFIED — rather than guessed at, so the gap is a named line somebody has to close rather than a silent pass.
components.licence: UNVERIFIED — no licence recorded anywhere in this tree (axllent/mailpit publishes MIT, but that claim was not checked here)
